title: unwrap_or_default ships an empty JWKS bundle instead of failing
description:
persona-grpc/src/service.rs:87-92, in `fetch_jwt_bundles`:

    let jwks_bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&b.jwt_authorities).unwrap_or_default();
    (b.trust_domain.to_string(), jwks_bytes)

On a serialisation failure the trust domain is still returned, paired with a zero-length byte string. A client receiving that sees a trust domain that exists but has no verification keys — indistinguishable from a trust domain legitimately configured with no JWT authorities. It will then reject every valid SVID from that domain and have no error to report.

`jwt_authorities` is a `serde_json::Value` (trust_bundle.rs:13), so `to_vec` fails only on a non-string map key or a float NaN/Inf reaching the store. Rare, but the failure mode is silent and the diagnosis ("why does verification suddenly fail for this domain") is expensive.

Fix: collect into `Result<Vec<_>, _>` and map a failure to `Status::internal`. A trust bundle the daemon cannot serialise is an internal error, not an empty bundle.

Related, same file: service.rs:156-158 uses `.unwrap_or_default()` on `SystemTime::duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)`, silently stamping `attested_at: 0` and `present_until: 300` (i.e. Jan 1 1970) into the token if the clock is pre-epoch. persona-core/src/signer.rs:98-100 handles the identical call with `.expect("system clock before epoch")`. Pick one treatment for the same invariant; the signer's is the right one.
close_reason: Duplicate of persona-5s4b.60 (same defect, filed by a second review agent from a different angle). Merged during review triage; reopen if the angle in this issue is not covered there.
